test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an example of the probability sampling technique?
solution:
The correct answer is** Purposive sampling.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Purposive sampling is NOT an example of the probability sampling technique:**

 
 
• Purposive sampling, also known as judgmental or subjective sampling, is a non-probability sampling technique where the researcher selects subjects based on specific characteristics or criteria. This method does not involve random selection, and the results cannot be generalized to the entire population.
 
• In a financial enterprise, purposive sampling might be used to select specific financial instruments or clients that meet certain criteria, such as high-net-worth individuals for a particular investment product.
 
• Since purposive sampling does not provide every member of the population with an equal chance of being selected, it is not considered a probability sampling technique.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stratified random sampling:**

 
 
• In stratified random sampling, the population is divided into distinct subgroups or strata, and random samples are taken from each stratum. This technique ensures representation from all subgroups, making it a probability sampling method.
 
 
 
• **Simple random sampling:**
 
 
• Simple random sampling involves selecting subjects from the population in such a way that every member has an equal chance of being chosen. This technique is the most straightforward form of probability sampling.
 
 
 
• **Systematic sampling:**
 
 
• Systematic sampling involves selecting every nth member of the population after a random start. This method ensures a degree of randomness and is considered a probability sampling technique.
